title: Prosocial Behaviour & Aggression
summary: Prosocial behaviour (helping, bystander effect, diffusion of responsibility) and aggression (frustration-aggression hypothesis). Causes and influences.
objectives: Explain the bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility.
revision: Prosocial behaviour and aggression: bystander effect, diffusion of responsibility, frustration-aggression hypothesis.
traps: Bystander effect = less help with others present (diffusion of responsibility).

notes.t: Voluntary behaviour intended to benefit another person, such as helping, sharing and cooperating.
Bystander Effect and Diffusion of Responsibility
The reduced likelihood of helping when other people are present, because responsibility is diffused among bystanders.
The phenomenon where each bystander assumes someone else will help, reducing any individual's sense of responsibility.
Behaviour intended to harm or injure another person who is motivated to avoid such treatment.
The proposal that frustration (blocking of goal-directed behaviour) creates a readiness to act aggressively.
UGC NET frequently asks about the bystander effect, diffusion of responsibility and the frustration-aggression hypothesis.

mnemonics.title: BFDA
mnemonics.text: B — Bystander effect (less help with others present), F — Frustration-aggression (blocked goals → aggression), D — Diffusion of responsibility, A — Aggression (harm intent)

flashcards.a: Less helping when others are present.
